message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering the 24-hour window ending 2026-07-07 05:10 IST (2026-07-06 23:40 UTC). Relevant new findings were identified for Ubuntu/OpenSSH/Python-related systems and Microsoft Edge mobile. No confirmed new MongoDB-family advisories were found in scope.

**Finding 1**

- Product: OpenSSH on Ubuntu 16.04 LTS
- Issue: CVE-2026-35385 / USN-8514-1
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu in the notice.
- Why it matters: Ubuntu published an OpenSSH notice on 6 July 2026 stating that OpenSSH could overwrite files as administrator. The affected package is `openssh`, and the issue could allow privilege escalation when downloading files as root with legacy scp behavior.
- Relevance: The monitored list includes both Ubuntu and OpenSSH.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8514-1

**Finding 2**

- Product: Python packages on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and 26.04 LTS
- Issue: USN-8509-1 covering multiple Python CVEs, including CVE-2026-9669, CVE-2026-8328, CVE-2026-6100, CVE-2026-6019, CVE-2026-5713, CVE-2026-4786, CVE-2026-4519, CVE-2026-4224, CVE-2026-3644, CVE-2026-3276, CVE-2026-2297, CVE-2026-1502, CVE-2026-1299, CVE-2025-69534, and CVE-2025-13462
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu in the notice.
- Why it matters: Ubuntu says several Python issues were fixed, including paths where crafted input could cause denial of service, header/content injection, SSRF, path restriction bypass, or possible arbitrary code execution in specific modules.
- Relevance: The monitored list includes Python and Ubuntu.
- Source: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8509-1

**Finding 3**

- Product: Ubuntu Linux kernel packages for NVIDIA and Raspberry Pi real-time variants
- Issue: USN-8507-1, USN-8508-1, and USN-8492-3 covering multiple kernel CVEs
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu in the notices.
- Why it matters: Ubuntu published multiple 6 July 2026 kernel notices for supported Ubuntu releases, including fixes across CPU, file system, network, GPU, SMB/NFS, and other kernel subsystems. Ubuntu describes possible system compromise for the NVIDIA kernel notices.
- Relevance: The monitored list includes Ubuntu, NFS, CIFS/SMB Utils, and NVIDIA CUDA-adjacent environments; this is most relevant where monitored Ubuntu hosts use these kernel flavors or related subsystems.
- Sources: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8507-1, https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8508-1, https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8492-3

**Finding 4**

- Product: Ubuntu core utilities and networking packages
- Issue: USN-8511-1 for socat (CVE-2026-56123, CVE-2024-54661), USN-8512-1 for gzip (CVE-2026-41991, CVE-2026-41992), and USN-8510-1 for tar (CVE-2025-45582)
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Ubuntu in the notices.
- Why it matters: Ubuntu published fixes for a socat SOCKS5 parser issue that could allow remote code execution, gzip issues that could allow file overwrite or information disclosure/denial of service, and a tar symlink extraction issue that could overwrite files.
- Relevance: The monitored list includes Ubuntu; these are Ubuntu package advisories for common system components.
- Sources: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8511-1, https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8512-1, https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8510-1

**Finding 5**

- Product: Microsoft Edge for Android and iOS
- Issue: July 6, 2026 Edge mobile security update, version 150.0.4078.50
- Severity: Not clearly stated; Microsoft says CVEs will be added when available.
- Why it matters: Microsoft released an Edge mobile update incorporating the latest Chromium security updates. CVE details were not yet listed at the time of review.
- Relevance: The monitored list includes Microsoft Edge.
- Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security

**Possible Matches Needing Review**

- ChromeOS / ChromeOS Flex stable update, 6 July 2026: Google published a ChromeOS stable update with browser version 149.0.7827.232, but the visible release note did not explicitly state security fixes or CVEs. Because the monitored product is Google Chrome rather than ChromeOS, this was not retained as a confirmed finding. Source: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Ubuntu systems running affected packages, especially OpenSSH, Python, socat, and the listed kernel variants. Edge mobile should be monitored for Microsoft CVE detail updates, since the July 6 release note says CVEs were not yet available.
